cases.expected: Message m contains a TSIGRecord with a standard (truncated) MAC and error code NOERROR
cases.description: Apply TSIG with a valid message and an existing TSIG record using the default (non‑full) signature. The method should generate a new TSIG RR, attach it to the message and set the MAC length to the default size.

cases.expected: Message m contains a TSIGRecord with a full‑length MAC (no truncation) and error code NOERROR
cases.description: Apply TSIG with the fullSignature flag set to true. The method should generate a TSIG RR that contains the complete MAC value rather than a truncated one.

group: Old TSIGRecord is null – generate new record

cases.expected: Message m contains a newly generated TSIGRecord (no old record to chain) and error code NOERROR
cases.description: When the old TSIGRecord argument is null the method must generate a fresh TSIG RR and attach it to the message.

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: Passing a null Message should cause the method to throw a NullPointerException because it cannot add a TSIG RR to a non‑existent message.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with message containing 'unsupported algorithm'
cases.description: If the old TSIGRecord contains an algorithm name that the TSIG class does not recognise, the method should reject the request and throw an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: Message m contains a TSIGRecord whose error field equals Rcode.FORMERR (or other non‑zero error code)
cases.description: When the internal call to apply(Message, int, TSIGRecord, boolean) is invoked with an error code other than NOERROR, the resulting TSIG RR must carry that error code.

group: Full signature requested but old record lacks MAC

cases.expected: IllegalStateException with message containing 'MAC missing'
cases.description: If fullSignature is true but the supplied old TSIGRecord does not contain a MAC (e.g., it is a placeholder), the method cannot compute a chain and must throw an IllegalStateException.

cases.expected: TSIGRecord attached to Message with error code Rcode.BADTIME
cases.description: If the timestamp in the message is older/newer than the current time by more than TSIG.FUDGE (300 s), the generated TSIG RR must indicate a BADTIME error.

group: Fudge boundary – timestamp exactly at upper limit

cases.expected: Message m contains a TSIGRecord with error code NOERROR (timestamp accepted at +300 s)
cases.description: The message timestamp is exactly the current time plus TSIG.FUDGE (300 s). The apply method must treat the timestamp as valid and generate a TSIG RR with NOERROR.

group: Fudge boundary – timestamp exactly at lower limit

cases.expected: Message m contains a TSIGRecord with error code NOERROR (timestamp accepted at –300 s)
cases.description: The message timestamp is exactly the current time minus TSIG.FUDGE (300 s). The apply method must accept the timestamp and generate a TSIG RR with NOERROR.

group: Fudge exceeded by one second – future timestamp

cases.expected: Message m contains a TSIGRecord with error code Rcode.BADTIME
cases.description: The message timestamp is 301 s in the future, i.e., just beyond the allowed fudge window. The apply method must set the error field to BADTIME.

group: Fudge exceeded by one second – past timestamp

cases.expected: Message m contains a TSIGRecord with error code Rcode.BADTIME
cases.description: The message timestamp is 301 s in the past, just outside the allowed fudge window. The apply method must set the error field to BADTIME.

group: Message already contains a TSIG – replacement

cases.expected: Message m contains exactly one TSIGRecord, the newly generated one (old TSIG replaced)
cases.description: When the message already has a TSIG RR, apply must remove the existing record and attach a freshly generated TSIG RR based on the supplied old record.

cases.expected: Generated TSIGRecord MAC length equals 10 bytes (default truncated size)
cases.description: The old TSIGRecord supplies a full‑length SHA‑1 MAC (20 bytes). With fullSignature set to false the apply method must truncate the MAC to the default 10‑byte length.

cases.expected: Generated TSIGRecord MAC length equals 20 bytes (full SHA‑1 MAC)
cases.description: When fullSignature is true the apply method must keep the complete MAC (no truncation). The resulting TSIG RR should contain the full 20‑byte SHA‑1 MAC.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with message containing 'secret key length'
cases.description: If the TSIGRecord references a secret key of zero length, the apply method cannot compute a MAC and must throw an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: Generated TSIGRecord MAC length equals 10 bytes (default truncated size) and algorithm name HMAC‑SHA256
cases.description: The old TSIGRecord uses the HMAC‑SHA256 algorithm. With fullSignature false the MAC must be truncated to the default 10‑byte size while preserving the algorithm identifier.

cases.expected: Generated TSIGRecord MAC length equals 32 bytes (full SHA‑256 MAC) and algorithm name HMAC‑SHA256
cases.description: When fullSignature is true and the algorithm is HMAC‑SHA256, the apply method must retain the full 32‑byte MAC.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with message containing 'secret key is null'
cases.description: The old TSIGRecord references a null secret key. The apply method must validate the key before MAC computation and throw an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException with message containing 'algorithm name is null'
cases.description: The supplied TSIGRecord has a null algorithm identifier. The method must reject such a record and raise an IllegalArgumentException.

group: Invalid secret key length for HMAC‑SHA256

cases.expected: GeneralSecurityException
cases.description: The old TSIGRecord specifies HMAC‑SHA256 but provides a secret key that is too short for the algorithm. When the MAC instance is initialized, the JCE provider throws a GeneralSecurityException, which should propagate from apply.

group: Unsupported MAC algorithm causing JCE failure

cases.expected: GeneralSecurityException
cases.description: The TSIGRecord uses a known algorithm name (e.g., HMAC‑SHA384) but the underlying JCE provider cannot supply a Mac instance for it, resulting in a GeneralSecurityException that must be thrown by apply.

cases.expected: IllegalStateException with message containing 'Message is immutable'
cases.description: When the Message instance is marked as immutable (e.g., after being sent), apply must refuse to modify it and throw an IllegalStateException.
